title: VPC Boundary Armor Terraform module (SG/NACL/PrivateDNS/Egress Gate)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reusable, idempotent Terraform module that encapsulates Redwood's recommended VPC boundary controls: stateful Security Groups, stateless NACLs for defense-in-depth, private hosted zones and conditional private DNS forwarding, and an egress policy layer that supports deny-by-default, approved destination lists, and per-customer overrides. The module must include versioning/upgrade guidance, migration helpers for existing stacks, and automated health checks (CloudWatch/Prometheus hooks) so Private customers can adopt hardened defaults with minimal operational lift.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes clear inputs for SG rules, NACL rules, and egress allowlists; defaults are secure deny-by-default
Private DNS integration supports creating private hosted zones and optional forwarding rules to customer resolvers without exposing public DNS
Egress policy supports tag-based exceptions and an allowlist file with checksum validation
Module is idempotent across repeated apply and safe for partial adoption (can be applied to subnets incrementally)
Automated health checks emit metrics for rule drift, denied-eps, and DNS resolution failures to the customer namespace
Terratest integration verifies module behavior in a sandbox AWS account and tests upgrade path between v1.0 and v1.1
Security review sign-off documented and any Sentinel/policy-as-code checks included in repo
technical_notes: Use provider-agnostic Terraform where possible but include an AWS-specific submodule (security_groups, network_acl, route53_private_zone, vpc_endpoint for resolver)
SGs implemented as least-privilege templates with allowlist mapping by service and port; attach descriptive tags for auditability
NACL rules generated from high-level intent (egress_allowlist, deny_private_to_public) to avoid rule ordering mistakes
Private DNS option creates a route53 private hosted zone and conditional forwarding to customer VPC resolver via resolver endpoints when requested
Egress enforcement pattern: sticky egress via NAT + egress proxy support where available; rules generate CloudWatch metrics for denied flows using VPC Flow Logs -> Lambda -> metrics
State migration: include a terraform import script and plan-check helper that surfaces destructive changes (changing NACL ordering, deleting SG references)
Health checks: lightweight Lambda that validates DNS resolution for all private zones and probes top-k allowed endpoints; emits prometheus-style metrics to the observability namespace
Module should support an opt-in "compat" mode that mirrors older naming conventions for backward compatibility during upgrades
Provide example usage patterns for single-tenant private deployment, multi-tenant Dedicated pools, and air-gapped on-prem mappings
implementation_plan: Define module API (inputs/outputs) and finalize defaults - week 1
Build AWS submodule (SG/NACL/Route53/Resolver) and local test harness - week 2
Add egress allowlist feature and checksum/validation logic; implement VPC Flow Log -> metric path - week 3
Implement health-check Lambda + CloudWatch metrics and alerting playbook - week 4
Add Terratest suite for create/upgrade/destroy scenarios and run in CI - week 5
Prepare migration helper scripts and write upgrade docs + rollout checklist - week 6
Security review, docs review, and final review with Platform and Customer Support - week 7
testing_plan: Unit tests for core helper functions (rule generation, allowlist parsing)
Terratest scenarios: apply baseline, assert expected SG/NACL entries, simulate traffic to verify egress deny, run upgrade to new module version and assert no destructive changes
Integration test: create private hosted zone, create forwarding to mock resolver, validate DNS resolution from an EC2 test instance
Chaos test: simulate partial apply failure and ensure idempotency on subsequent runs
Security fuzz: inject malformed allowlist entries and assert module rejects with clear error messages
rollout_plan: Publish v0.1-beta module to internal registry and announce to PMC and Solutions Engineering
Onboard 2 pilot customers (one Dedicated, one Private VPC) with Platform ENG support and monitor metrics for 72h
Iterate on pilot feedback, fix issues, then tag v1.0 and publish public docs
Provide migration guide and `terraform import` helper for existing customers; offer limited migration support for enterprise customers
After v1.0, enable optional auto-remediation playbooks in Console for drift detection

T7: Security review and policy-as-code checks (Sentinel/OPA)
